reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-documented urban legend and scientifically false. Neuroscience research, including functional neuroimaging techniques like fMRI and PET scans, demonstrates that virtually all areas of the brain show activity and are engaged across different tasks throughout the day. Furthermore, from an evolutionary and physiological standpoint, brain tissue that remains unused typically atrophies, and the brain consumes roughly 20% of the body's energy, which would be evolutionary non-viable if 90% were dormant. Sources such as the MIT McGovern Institute, Scientific American, and Psychology Today confirm this is a persistent myth.
title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
